name: cncjs
summary: Web-based CNC machine control interface for G-code streaming, monitoring, and operator workflows.
why_it_matters: CNCjs captures useful machine-control capability knowledge for fabrication scenarios, but hardware coupling and zero current usage make it a blueprint rather than an actively maintained resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs browser-based CNC control and job execution.
Operators need machine status, G-code streaming, or manufacturing automation.
The workflow depends on integrating hobby or light industrial CNC controllers.

platform_support.notes: The web app can run in containers across platforms, but useful operation depends on USB or serial access to host-connected CNC hardware.

prerequisites: Clear operator safety and machine ownership model
implementation_notes: Keep any future support narrow and hardware-tested.
Promotion should define how machine profiles and macros are stored.
Treat machine control and job planning as separate concerns.
operational_notes: Hardware access and permissions are the main support constraint.
Recovery behavior after controller disconnects must be explicit.
Health checks should validate connectivity to the controller, not only the web UI.
risks: Machine-control integrations have real safety consequences.
A generic wrapper would overpromise portability and reliability.
